item.text: {"question_id":"4B.3","answer":"In 2023, the legal framework contained some protections: the constitution provided for peaceful assembly and association, and the revised press law added access to some public-interest information. However, the press revision retained prison exposure and broad restrictions, while authorities used defamation, insult, contempt, and false-information provisions against critics and journalists. In practice, opposition and civic freedoms were repeatedly restricted. Authorities limited opposition demonstrations, used excessive or deadly force—including the planned Goma operation in which security forces killed at least 56 people according to the official count, injured more than 80, and arbitrarily arrested more than 150—and arrested or detained opposition figures, activists, satirists, and journalists. Police violently dispersed the May Kinshasa opposition march, while the president congratulated the police chief who oversaw it, despite an announced investigation. Journalists faced threats, physical attacks, self-censorship, broadcaster restrictions, and prosecution; Bujakera remained in pretrial detention during the reported period over charges tied to a report he reportedly did not write. Tshisekedi publicly said criticism concerning human-rights violations or deprivation of freedoms would not change his security position. His stated refusal to intervene in Bujakera’s case can be read as a separation-of-powers position, but it did not establish an effective remedy or judicial independence in practice. There was contrary evidence: Diongo was released without charge, three officers were detained after the May march, four officers were convicted in connection with the Goma killings, the government condemned some attacks, and police escorted a peaceful October Goma march. These corrective or permissive instances were partial and did not demonstrate reliable protection, accountability, or remedy. Attribution to Tshisekedi is strongest for his public statements and praise of the Kinshasa police operation; most arrests, attacks, and protest operations are attributable to state authorities or ruling-party supporters under his government, but the supplied record does not establish his personal order for each act. Some abuses also involved opposition actors, armed groups, or other non-state forces, and Goma casualty figures and investigation outcomes remain contested or incomplete.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0011-E018","BATCH-0002-E011","BATCH-0003-E010","BATCH-0010-E013","BATCH-0025-E007","BATCH-0025-E008","BATCH-0025-E012","BATCH-0027-E002"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0003-E007","BATCH-0011-E011","BATCH-0022-E014","BATCH-0025-E013","BATCH-0027-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The supplied evidence does not establish Tshisekedi’s direct order for most arrests, attacks, or protest operations; responsibility higher in the chain of command was not fully adjudicated.","The record does not establish whether all announced investigations, prosecutions, or promised remedies produced final, effective accountability.","The evidence aggregates conduct by government and non-state actors and does not show whether the October escorted protest reflected a consistent national practice.","The press-law and Bujakera evidence documents formal rules and proceedings but does not establish the full judicial interpretation or final outcome."],"corrections_made":["Removed the unsupported characterization of the revised press law and election-audit arrangements as effective formal protections.","Added Tshisekedi’s June statement that criticism of human-rights violations or deprivation of freedoms would not alter his security position.","Added his stated non-intervention in Bujakera’s case, while preserving the distinction between separation-of-powers rhetoric and effective remedy.","Preserved the strongest favorable evidence: Diongo’s release without charge, police escort of the October Goma march, officer arrests or convictions, and official condemnations.","Qualified the Goma casualty figures, attribution, non-state violence, and incomplete accountability record."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":[]}
